notes:
POC story: migrating from incumbent LLM API (prod usage today) -> Redwood Hosted (compat layer) -> Dedicated. Key priorities: prompt parity, no-regression on escalation templates, predictable SLOs, cost savings.

Key quotes / call excerpts:
- 'We need a drop-in path; can't rewrite 1000+ prompts overnight.' — Head of Product
- 'If you can show consistent latency and ~30% token-cost reduction at our scale we'd consider a 12 month Dedicated commit.' — CFO paraphrase

Technical/POC details and findings:
- Compatibility shim implemented by RailCrest engineering to translate existing OpenAI-style calls to Redwood Hosted endpoints. Worked for ~85% of traffic with small header tweaks.
- Regression window: 12 unique prompt templates triggered shorter/less precise escalation instructions on Redwood's hosted default model. SE team reproduced with A/B harness.
- Root cause suspected: model variant + temperature default mismatch + tokenization differences; suggested mitigation: consistent model pinning and prompt canonicalization layer on their side or use Redwood's templating hooks.
- Latency: hosted median for chat context (1–3 turns) = 90ms/token; incumbent median = 80ms/token. P95 for hosted spikes to 260ms under bursty QPS — Dedicated expected to smooth this.
- Cost: preliminary token-unit calc shows ~25–35% lower cost using Redwood recommended batching/caching profiles vs incumbent at current workload shapes.

Operational asks from RailCrest:
- Clear guidance on model mapping and a compatibility matrix (OpenAI -> Redwood model equivalents).
- Canary rollout recipe for Dedicated: canary %s, health checks, automatic fallback to hosted if performance degrades.
- Audit log retention options (90/365/730 days) and KMS key rotation policy documentation.

Short-term next actions (AE/SE):
- Provide a short runbook for prompt parity checks (probe suite + expected signals).
- Schedule Dedicated POC calendar and define SLA targets for the reserved pool.
- Send SOC2 package and legal terms summary.

Longer-term: if Dedicated POC passes, RailCrest plans a phased migration: 20% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 6–8 weeks, with rollback windows.
